| Point to | Attachment |

7.05.b:
### ACL
[[FIG: Fig 7.18, 7.19 · 7.05
| Item | ACL |
|---|---|
| Bundles | **AM** (tight in flexion) + **PL** (tight in extension) → named by tibial site |
| Function | Primary restraint to **anterior tibial translation**; PL → rotation (pivot shift) |
| Blood | **Middle genicular** artery |

- X-ray → normal ACL parallel to or steeper than **Blumensaat line**

### PCL
[[FIG: Fig 7.20 · 7.05
| Item | PCL |
|---|---|
| Tibia | Posterior intercondylar fossa → **≈1–1.5 cm below** joint line |
| Bundles | **AL** (anterolateral) (larger, stronger, tight in flexion) + **PM** (posteromedial) (tight in extension) |
| Meniscofemoral | **Humphrey** → anterior to PCL; **Wrisberg** → posterior to PCL |
| Function | Primary restraint to **posterior tibial translation** |
| Danger | Popliteal artery ≈7 mm behind the footprint → farther in flexion |

- Tibial landmark → **champagne-glass drop-off** → guide-pin target

HIGH YIELD
- PCL → ≈30% larger and stronger than ACL · fails at ≈2500–3000 N vs MCL ≈800, LCL ≈400 N → LCL weakest
- Single-bundle PCL reconstruction → **AL bundle**
- Both cruciates → intra-articular but **extrasynovial**
- ACL does **not** heal → sheath tears, synovial fluid stops the clot, poorer blood supply
- **PCL** may heal → better supply, thicker sheath

7.10.t: Popliteal Fossa, Vessels & the Anastomosis Around the Knee
7.10.b:
### Boundaries & contents
| Boundary | Formed by |
|---|---|
| **Superomedial** | Semimembranosus + semitendinosus |
| **Superolateral** | Biceps femoris |
| **Inferior** | Two heads of gastrocnemius (+ plantaris laterally) |

- Contents, **back → front** → tibial nerve → popliteal vein → **popliteal artery (deepest, on bone)**
  [[FIG: Fig 7.35 · 7.10
- CPN (common peroneal nerve) → along **medial border of biceps** → leaves the fossa laterally

### Popliteal artery
- Starts → **adductor hiatus** · ends → lower border of **popliteus** → anterior tibial + tibioperoneal trunk
  [[FIG: Fig 7.36 · 7.10
- **Tethered** at both ends (hiatus + soleal arch) → stretched in **knee dislocation**
  - Rule → measure **ABI** (ankle–brachial index); <0.9 → CT angiography
- Behind the posterior tibia → flexion does **not** move it away

### Anastomosis around the knee
- **9 arteries** → 2 from above + 4 genicular from the popliteal + 3 from below · middle genicular → cruciates, not the ring
  [[FIG: Fig 7.37 · 7.10

| From | Artery | Course / point to say |
|---|---|---|
| **Above** | **Descending genicular** (femoral, in the adductor canal) | Articular branch → medial side |
| | **Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral** (profunda) | Down along vastus lateralis → lateral side |
| **Popliteal** | **Superior medial / lateral genicular** | Just above the condyles; **superior lateral genicular artery** → lateral release |
| | **Middle genicular** | Pierces the OPL → **cruciates + synovium**; not counted in the ring |
| | **Inferior medial genicular** | Below the medial condyle, **deep to the sMCL** |
| | **Inferior lateral genicular** | Along the **lateral joint line**, deep to the FCL (between the laminae of layer 3) |
| **Below** | **Anterior tibial recurrent** (anterior tibial) | Up through tibialis anterior → front of the knee |
| | **Posterior tibial recurrent** | Small, behind the popliteus |
| | **Circumflex fibular** | Round the fibular neck, with the CPN |

- Two planes → **superficial** (in front of patella + patellar tendon) + **deep** (on bone and capsule) · **patellar ring** between them
- Function → collateral flow round a **slowly** occluded popliteal artery + blood supply of the patella

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "describe the anastomosis around the knee"
- From above → **descending genicular** (femoral) + **descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral** (profunda)
- From the popliteal → **superior medial, superior lateral, inferior medial, inferior lateral** genicular (middle → cruciates only)
- From below → **anterior tibial recurrent, posterior tibial recurrent, circumflex fibular**
- Superficial + deep network → **patellar ring** → blood of the patella
- Importance → patella in total knee arthroplasty (TKA: medial arthrotomy + lateral release), HTO (high tibial osteotomy)
  - Too weak after **acute** popliteal injury → knee dislocation = vascular emergency

PITFALL — parent artery of two branches
- Gray's → **posterior tibial recurrent** from the **anterior tibial**, **circumflex fibular** from the **posterior tibial** · Netter's table → the other way round
- Give Gray's and add "some atlases differ"

### Blood supply of the patella
- **Extraosseous** → patellar ring (mainly the four genicular + descending genicular + anterior tibial recurrent)
- **Intraosseous**
  - 1 · **Midpatellar** vessels → middle third of the anterior surface
  - 2 · **Polar** vessels → into the **apex (inferior pole)**, behind the patellar tendon
- Flow **inferior → superior** → transverse fracture → **proximal fragment** can lose its supply → AVN (avascular necrosis)
